releases.notes:
Fourth release of the mod and desktop app. Litescape now runs on every Minecraft version Litematica supports, from 1.21.1 to 26.3, on Fabric Loader 0.20.1+.

Minecraft versions:
- One jar per Litematica release line, covering 1.21.1 through 26.3 (#67).

Farms and portals:
- Farm parts connect across dimensions, the viewer checks where their portals lead, and spawning is judged per dimension (#71).
- The Portals panel follows a portal to where it lands (#74).

Fixes:
- Sharing over your own share merges the two instead of listing both (#76).

Desktop app:
- Windows ARM, .deb and .rpm builds (#65).
- A pixel-art icon for the app and the mod (#68).

Also: a project website with a live demo of the viewer (#78, #79), and a shorter README (#69).

Install: `brew install --cask GA16-24/tap/litescape` (or download the app below) and click Install next to your Fabric instance. Without the app, put the `litescape-0.3.2+<minecraft version>.jar` that matches your game and Fabric API in `mods/` along with Litematica and MaLiLib. The same jar works on a server.

mods.name: Litescape
mods.description: View your Litematica or BuildPrint area selection and placements as live 3D models in your browser. Install on the server too for full-range data in multiplayer.

releases.notes:
Third release of the mod and desktop app, for Minecraft 26.3 on Fabric Loader 0.20.1+.

Sharing:
- A shared schematic now arrives as a request that the other player accepts or denies (#45).
- Shared schematics load into Litematica at their coordinates, with chest and hopper contents (#43).
- The owner can leave designer notes on a shared schematic (#58).

Building:
- An Order layer mode steps through a survival build order one stage at a time (#62).
- Redstone components that are set up wrong are listed apart from cosmetic mismatches (#55), and the viewer says when a build's redstone and containers are ready to activate (#53).
- The materials list counts shulker boxes (#47).
- The viewer shows which biomes and Y levels a build covers (#56), marks the blocks mobs can spawn on (#59), and gives the matching Nether or Overworld coordinates for portal linking (#51).

Viewer and app:
- The viewer is translated into 9 languages and follows the player's language (#37).
- A settings page in the viewer, and a Settings window in the desktop app (#35).
- The desktop app installs Fabric API, MaLiLib and Litematica along with the mod, keeps the mod updated in every instance, and can create a Litescape instance for the Minecraft Launcher (#34).
- Joined servers are remembered per Minecraft account rather than per instance (#42).
- BuildPrint builds and selections can be read like Litematica placements (#39).

Fixes:
- Shader options set to a name are no longer forced to 0 (#49).
- Bloom in Bliss no longer reads blue noise instead of the bloom buffer (#60).

Install: `brew install --cask GA16-24/tap/litescape` (or download the app below) and click Install next to your Fabric 26.3 instance. Without the app, put `litescape-0.3.0.jar` and Fabric API in `mods/` along with Litematica 0.29.1 and MaLiLib. The same jar works on a server.

mods.name: Litescape
mods.description: View your Litematica area selection as a live 3D model in your browser. Install on the server too for full-range data in multiplayer.

releases.notes:
Second release of the mod, for Minecraft 26.3 on Fabric Loader 0.20.1+.

Changes since 0.1.0:
- The mod is now called Litescape everywhere, including in-game and in the viewer (#27).
- The side panel's dropdowns and buttons stay open and take clicks instead of resetting on every poll (#25).
- Glass windows no longer blow out into a white blob with MakeUp (#17).
- Complementary on Ultra no longer shows a World Space Reflections error (#26).

Install it the same way as 0.1.0: put the jar and Fabric API in `mods/` on the client (with Litematica 0.29.1 and MaLiLib) and, optionally, on the server. One jar works on both sides.
